gruplar.cloze-a: Honeybees play a vital role in agriculture, (17) ---- roughly one third of the food crops we eat. In recent decades, however, beekeepers in many countries (18) ---- unusually high losses of their colonies. Scientists have identified several factors behind this decline, (19) ---- pesticide use, parasites and the loss of wild flowers. (20) ----, they still disagree about which of these factors is the most important. Protecting bees will therefore require coordinated action by farmers and governments, as well as changes in the way land (21) ----.
gruplar.cloze-b: Sleep is not simply a period of rest; it is an active state (22) ---- the brain carries out essential maintenance. During deep sleep, for example, waste products that build up during the day (23) ---- from the brain more efficiently. Researchers have also found that sleep helps to strengthen memories, (24) ---- explains why people who sleep well after learning something new tend to recall it better. Despite this, many adults regularly get less sleep than they need, (25) ---- because of long working hours or the use of electronic devices late at night. Experts recommend that adults aim for seven to nine hours a night, although individual needs may (26) ---- considerably.
gruplar.okuma-1: Cities are often several degrees warmer than the surrounding countryside, a phenomenon known as the urban heat island effect. The main reason is that materials such as asphalt and concrete absorb heat during the day and release it slowly at night. In addition, cities have fewer trees and less vegetation, which would otherwise cool the air through evaporation. Waste heat from cars, air conditioners and factories adds to the problem. The effect is not merely uncomfortable; during heatwaves it can be deadly, particularly for elderly people and those with heart conditions. Fortunately, there are practical ways to reduce it. Painting roofs white, for example, reflects sunlight instead of absorbing it, while planting trees provides both shade and cooling. Some cities have also begun to replace traditional pavements with materials that allow water to soak into the ground, which helps to keep surfaces cooler.
gruplar.okuma-2: Octopuses are widely regarded as the most intelligent invertebrates. They can solve puzzles, open jars to reach food and even escape from tanks in aquariums. What makes this intelligence remarkable is that it evolved independently from that of mammals and birds. The last common ancestor of octopuses and humans was a simple worm-like creature that lived more than 500 million years ago. Unlike vertebrates, octopuses have most of their neurons not in their brain but in their eight arms, which can taste, touch and even make some decisions on their own. Researchers believe that this unusual nervous system may have developed because octopuses need to control flexible bodies with no bones. However, their intelligence comes with a surprising limitation: most species live for only one to two years, which means they have little time to learn from experience.
gruplar.okuma-3: The placebo effect occurs when a patient's condition improves after receiving a treatment that has no active ingredients, such as a sugar pill. For a long time, doctors viewed this effect as a nuisance that made it harder to test new drugs. In clinical trials, a new medicine must perform better than a placebo before it can be approved, because some patients in the placebo group almost always report feeling better. More recently, however, scientists have started to study the placebo effect as a phenomenon in its own right. Brain imaging studies show that expecting relief can trigger the release of natural painkillers in the brain. Interestingly, the effect seems to be stronger when the treatment looks more serious: injections tend to work better than pills, and two pills work better than one. Some researchers now wonder whether doctors could use these findings to improve the care they provide without deceiving their patients.
gruplar.okuma-4: Before 2020, working from home was a privilege enjoyed by a relatively small number of employees. The pandemic changed this almost overnight, as millions of office workers were sent home and companies discovered that many jobs could be done remotely. Surveys suggest that most employees now value the flexibility of working from home at least part of the time, mainly because it saves them the time and cost of commuting. Employers' views are more mixed. While some report higher productivity and lower office costs, others worry that remote work weakens team spirit and makes it harder to train new staff. As a result, many organisations have adopted a hybrid model, in which employees spend some days in the office and others at home. Whether this compromise will last is still unclear, but it seems unlikely that the traditional five-day office week will return for everyone.
gruplar.okuma-5: Coffee is thought to have originated in Ethiopia, where, according to a popular legend, a goat herder noticed that his animals became unusually energetic after eating the berries of a certain plant. Whether or not the story is true, by the fifteenth century coffee was being grown in Yemen, and from there it spread throughout the Middle East. Coffee houses soon became important social centres where people met to talk, listen to music and discuss the news. In the seventeenth century, coffee reached Europe, where it was at first regarded with suspicion; some critics even called it a dangerous drink. Nevertheless, its popularity grew rapidly, and coffee houses in cities such as London and Vienna became places where merchants, writers and scientists exchanged ideas. Today, coffee is one of the most widely traded agricultural products in the world, grown in more than seventy countries.
